interpretationNotes: Original Masoretic relative-year sequence retained; Ussher BC is a model overlay, not the biblical calendar.

genealogyViews.title: Ruth 4: Perez to David
interpretationNotes: Names reflect reported succession; not all genealogical lists guarantee every intervening generation.

genealogyViews.title: Matthew 1: Abraham to Joseph, then Mary and Jesus
interpretationNotes: Matthew uses a structured genealogical presentation with omitted generations elsewhere in the historical record. Edges represent ancestry as listed, not guaranteed adjacent biological generations.
Joseph is the husband of Mary; Matthew 1:16 states Jesus was born of Mary, not begotten biologically by Joseph.
A continuous tree from Adam through Genesis and Matthew can be projected from linked paths, with its textual gaps labeled.

genealogyViews.title: Luke 3: Adam to Joseph (qualified), then Jesus
interpretationNotes: Scriptural line as Luke states it. Luke 3:23 does not explicitly identify this as Mary’s genealogy.
Luke includes Cainan between Arphaxad and Shelah whereas Genesis 11 in the Masoretic text omits that generation. Retain both text witnesses rather than blending the chronology models.
The parent named for Joseph differs: Matthew lists Jacob; Luke lists Heli. The distinction is source-specific; it is not automatically harmonized.
Person mentions sharing a name are kept separate until identity is independently established, especially Shealtiel and Zerubbabel across the two paths.

genealogyViews.title: From Adam to Jesus: Genesis + Matthew ancestry view
interpretationNotes: Combined projection, not a separately printed contiguous genealogy; Matthew provides the Abraham-to-Jesus portion.
